claim: Malaria causes an estimated 405,000 deaths annually.
source: Despite extensive biomedical and public health measures, malaria persists as a major global health concern, with an estimated 405,000 deaths and 228 million cases annually (WHO, 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to WHO, 2019.

claim: Malaria causes an estimated 228 million cases annually.
source: Despite extensive biomedical and public health measures, malaria persists as a major global health concern, with an estimated 405,000 deaths and 228 million cases annually (WHO, 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to WHO, 2019.

claim: Resistant strains have been detected against all currently available antimalarial drugs, including sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine, mefloquine, halofantrine, quinine, and artemisinin.
source: Moreover, resistant strains have been detected against all currently available antimalarial drugs, including sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine, mefloquine, halofantrine, quinine, and artemisinin (Cui et al., 2015; Ross and Fidock, 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Cui et al., 2015 and Ross and Fidock, 2019.

claim: Approximately 94% of malaria deaths are caused by Plasmodium falciparum.
source: Although ~94% of deaths are caused by Plasmodium falciparum (Pf) (WHO, 2019), other Plasmodium species that infect humans (P. vivax, P. malariae, P. knowlesi and P. ovale) also cause debilitating disease and have been associated with fatal outcomes (Lover et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to WHO, 2019.

claim: Other Plasmodium species that infect humans (P. vivax, P. malariae, P. knowlesi and P. ovale) cause debilitating disease and have been associated with fatal outcomes.
source: Although ~94% of deaths are caused by Plasmodium falciparum (Pf) (WHO, 2019), other Plasmodium species that infect humans (P. vivax, P. malariae, P. knowlesi and P. ovale) also cause debilitating disease and have been associated with fatal outcomes (Lover et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lover et al., 2018.

claim: During a blood meal, sporozoites are deposited into the skin of a host organism from the salivary glands of a mosquito.
source: During a blood meal, sporozoites are deposited into the skin of a host organism from the salivary glands of a mosquito, and subsequently migrate through the bloodstream to infect host hepatocytes (de Koning-Ward et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to de Koning-Ward et al., 2015.

claim: Sporozoites subsequently migrate through the bloodstream to infect host hepatocytes.
source: During a blood meal, sporozoites are deposited into the skin of a host organism from the salivary glands of a mosquito, and subsequently migrate through the bloodstream to infect host hepatocytes (de Koning-Ward et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to de Koning-Ward et al., 2015.

claim: The pre-erythrocytic sporozoite stage of the Plasmodium life cycle has long been considered a promising target for the development of an anti-malarial vaccine.
source: Due to the small number of parasites transmitted and the expression of protein antigens that possess conserved functional regions (Rosenberg et al., 1990; Smith et al., 2014), the pre-erythrocytic sporozoite stage of the Plasmodium life cycle has long been considered a promising target for the development of an anti-malarial vaccine (Nussenzweig and Nussenzweig, 1984).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Rosenberg et al., 1990; Smith et al., 2014; and Nussenzweig and Nussenzweig, 1984.

claim: Circumsporozoite protein (CSP) is the most abundant protein on the surface of Plasmodium sporozoites.
source: Circumsporozoite protein (CSP) is the most abundant protein on the surface of Plasmodium sporozoites, and is necessary for parasite development in mosquitoes and establishment of infection in host liver cells (Cerami et al., 1992; Frevert et al., 1993; Ménard et al., 1997).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Cerami et al., 1992; Frevert et al., 1993; Ménard et al., 1997.

claim: CSP is necessary for parasite development in mosquitoes and establishment of infection in host liver cells.
source: Circumsporozoite protein (CSP) is the most abundant protein on the surface of Plasmodium sporozoites, and is necessary for parasite development in mosquitoes and establishment of infection in host liver cells (Cerami et al., 1992; Frevert et al., 1993; Ménard et al., 1997).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Cerami et al., 1992; Frevert et al., 1993; Ménard et al., 1997.

claim: CSP contains an unusual central region consisting of multiple, short (4 to 8) amino acid repeats.
source: Flanked by N- and C-terminal domains, CSP contains an unusual central region consisting of multiple, short (4 to 8) amino acid (aa) repeats (Eichinger et al., 1986; Dame et al., 1984; Plassmeyer et al., 2009; Zavala et al., 1983).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Eichinger et al., 1986; Dame et al., 1984; Plassmeyer et al., 2009; Zavala et al., 1983.

claim: The sequence of the CSP repeating motif depends on the Plasmodium species and field isolate.
source: The sequence of the repeating motif depends on the Plasmodium species and field isolate (Chenet et al., 2012; Rich et al., 2000; Tahar et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Chenet et al., 2012; Rich et al., 2000; Tahar et al., 1998.

claim: The central region of CSP is highly immunodominant.
source: Importantly, the central region of CSP is highly immunodominant and antibodies targeting the repeats can inhibit sporozoite infectivity by preventing parasite migration (Mishra et al., 2012) and attachment to hepatocytes (Potocnjak et al., 1980; Yoshida et al., 1980).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Mishra et al., 2012; Potocnjak et al., 1980; Yoshida et al., 1980.

claim: Antibodies targeting the CSP repeats can inhibit sporozoite infectivity by preventing parasite migration.
source: Importantly, the central region of CSP is highly immunodominant and antibodies targeting the repeats can inhibit sporozoite infectivity by preventing parasite migration (Mishra et al., 2012) and attachment to hepatocytes (Potocnjak et al., 1980; Yoshida et al., 1980).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Mishra et al., 2012.

claim: Antibodies targeting the CSP repeats can inhibit sporozoite infectivity by preventing attachment to hepatocytes.
source: Importantly, the central region of CSP is highly immunodominant and antibodies targeting the repeats can inhibit sporozoite infectivity by preventing parasite migration (Mishra et al., 2012) and attachment to hepatocytes (Potocnjak et al., 1980; Yoshida et al., 1980).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Potocnjak et al., 1980; Yoshida et al., 1980.

claim: PfCSP is a major component of the leading malaria vaccine RTS,S/AS01.
source: PfCSP is a major component of the leading malaria vaccine RTS,S/AS01, which is currently undergoing pilot implementation in Africa (Adepoju, 2019; Draper et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Adepoju, 2019; Draper et al., 2018.

claim: RTS,S/AS01 is currently undergoing pilot implementation in Africa.
source: PfCSP is a major component of the leading malaria vaccine RTS,S/AS01, which is currently undergoing pilot implementation in Africa (Adepoju, 2019; Draper et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Adepoju, 2019; Draper et al., 2018.

claim: Anti-PfCSP repeat antibodies have been suggested to form the predominant humoral immune response elicited by RTS,S/AS01.
source: Anti-PfCSP repeat antibodies have been suggested to form the predominant humoral immune response elicited by RTS,S/AS01, and correlate with vaccine efficacy (Dobaño et al., 2019; McCall et al., 2018; Olotu et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Dobaño et al., 2019; McCall et al., 2018; Olotu et al., 2016.

claim: Anti-PfCSP repeat antibodies correlate with RTS,S/AS01 vaccine efficacy.
source: Anti-PfCSP repeat antibodies have been suggested to form the predominant humoral immune response elicited by RTS,S/AS01, and correlate with vaccine efficacy (Dobaño et al., 2019; McCall et al., 2018; Olotu et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Dobaño et al., 2019; McCall et al., 2018; Olotu et al., 2016.

claim: RTS,S/AS01 offers only modest and short-lived protection.
source: However, RTS,S/AS01 offers only modest and short-lived protection (RTS,S Clinical Trials Partnership, 2015; RTS,S Clinical Trials Partnership et al., 2012; RTS,S Clinical Trials Partnership et al., 2011); thus, it is critical to develop a better molecular understanding of the antibody response against this Plasmodium antigen, particularly the repeat region (Davies et al., 2015; Doolan, 2011; Illingworth et al., 2019), to obtain valuable information needed for improved vaccine design.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to RTS,S Clinical Trials Partnership, 2015; RTS,S Clinical Trials Partnership et al., 2012; RTS,S Clinical Trials Partnership et al., 2011.

claim: mAb 3D11 was isolated from mice exposed to the bites of mosquitoes that had been infected with γ-irradiated Pb parasites.
source: For example, mAb 3D11 was isolated from mice exposed to the bites of mosquitoes that had been infected with γ-irradiated Pb parasites (Yoshida et al., 1980).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Yoshida et al., 1980.

claim: mAb 3D11 recognition of the PbCSP central repeat region on the surface of live sporozoites resulted in abolished Pb infectivity in vitro and in vivo.
source: mAb 3D11 recognition of the PbCSP central repeat region on the surface of live sporozoites resulted in abolished Pb infectivity in vitro and in vivo (Cochrane et al., 1976).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Cochrane et al., 1976.

claim: Electron micrographs of Pb sporozoites pre-treated with mAb 3D11 revealed the presence of amorphous, precipitated material on the parasite surface characteristic of the circumsporozoite precipitation reaction.
source: Electron micrographs of Pb sporozoites pre-treated with mAb 3D11 revealed the presence of amorphous, precipitated material on the parasite surface characteristic of the circumsporozoite precipitation reaction (Yoshida et al., 1980).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Yoshida et al., 1980.

claim: A recent study used mAb 3D11 in combination with transmission-blocking mAb 4B7 to show that antibody targeting of both the pre-erythrocytic and sexual stages of a Pfs25-transgenic Pb parasite led to a synergistic reduction of parasite transmission in mice.
source: For example, a recent study used mAb 3D11 in combination with transmission-blocking mAb 4B7 to show that antibody targeting of both the pre-erythrocytic and sexual stages of a Pfs25-transgenic Pb parasite led to a synergistic reduction of parasite transmission in mice (Sherrard-Smith et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sherrard-Smith et al., 2018.

claim: The central repeats of PfCSP and PbCSP consist of recurring 4-aa motifs rich in asparagine and proline residues.
source: The central repeats of PfCSP and PbCSP consist of recurring 4-aa motifs rich in asparagine and proline residues (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Figure 1A which shows the schematic representations and sequences of PfCSP and PbCSP.

claim: PfCSP is composed of repeating NANP motifs interspersed with intermittent NVDP repeats, and a singular NPDP motif in the junction immediately following the N-terminal domain.
source: PfCSP is composed of repeating NANP motifs interspersed with intermittent NVDP repeats, and a singular NPDP motif in the junction immediately following the N-terminal domain.
evidence: The claim is supported by the description in the text and Figure 1A.

claim: Numerous reports have identified NPNA as the structurally relevant unit of the PfCSP central region.
source: While the major repeat motif of PfCSP is often referred to as NANP, numerous reports have identified NPNA as the structurally relevant unit of the central region (Kisalu et al., 2018; Oyen et al., 2017; Dyson et al., 1990; Ghasparian et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kisalu et al., 2018; Oyen et al., 2017; Dyson et al., 1990; Ghasparian et al., 2006.

claim: The central domain of PbCSP contains an array of PPPP and PAPP motifs interspersed with NPND or NAND motifs.
source: Similarly, the central domain of PbCSP contains an array of PPPP and PAPP motifs interspersed with NPND or NAND motifs (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Figure 1A which shows the schematic representation and sequence of PbCSP.

claim: Both PfCSP and PbCSP orthologs contain the conserved pentamer, KLKQP, known as Region I, at the C-terminal end of the N-terminal domain.
source: Notably, both orthologs contain the conserved pentamer, KLKQP, known as Region I, at the C-terminal end of the N-terminal domain.
evidence: The claim is supported by the description in the text and Figure 1A.

claim: All eight CSP peptides (four from PfCSP and four from PbCSP) were highly disordered and adopted a large ensemble of conformations with low to moderate secondary structure propensities.
source: Each simulation was conducted in water for a total production time of 18 μs. All eight peptides were highly disordered and adopted a large ensemble of conformations with low to moderate secondary structure propensities (Figure 1B and E), which are best described in statistical terms.
evidence: The claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 1B and E.

claim: The only secondary structure observed in the CSP peptides was local, and consisted of sparse, transient hydrogen-bonded turns.
source: The only secondary structure observed was local, and consisted of sparse, transient hydrogen-bonded turns (Figure 1C and F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 2, and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 1C, F, and supplementary figures.

claim: β-turns were the most populated secondary structure in the CSP peptides (up to 40%).
source: In particular, these interactions consisted of forward α-, β-, and γ-turns, with the β-turns being the most populated (up to 40%; Figure 1C and F), consistent with previous NMR studies focused on the NANP repeats (Dyson et al., 1990).
evidence: The claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 1C and F, and is consistent with previous NMR studies cited.

claim: Across all peptides, the average β-turn lifetime ranged from 2.7 ± 0.2 ns for the Pb PPNA turn to 4.4 ± 0.4 ns for DPNA turns found within PfCSP.
source: Across all peptides, the average β-turn lifetime ranged from 2.7 ± 0.2 ns for the Pb PPNA turn to 4.4 ± 0.4 ns for DPNA turns found within PfCSP (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data reported in Supplementary file 1.

claim: Each individual motif consistently exhibited the same structural tendencies, independent of their position and the overall peptide sequence in which they were contained.
source: Importantly, each individual motif consistently exhibited the same structural tendencies, independent of their position and the overall peptide sequence in which they were contained (Figure 1C and F, and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 1C, F, and Supplementary file 1.

claim: The presence of an intramolecular hydrogen bond in one motif does not alter the hydrogen-bonding propensities of adjacent motifs.
source: Furthermore, using the probability rule stating that two events are independent if the equation P(A∩B)=P(A)·P(B) holds true, we show that the presence of an intramolecular hydrogen bond in one motif does not alter the hydrogen-bonding propensities of adjacent motifs (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data and mathematical analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B and C.

claim: In both PfCSP and PbCSP, there is no discernable cooperativity between the structures of different repeat motifs.
source: Therefore, in both PfCSP and PbCSP we conclude that there is no discernable cooperativity between the structures of different repeat motifs, and as such, in the absence of extended or nonlocal secondary structure, each of these motifs behaves as an independent unit with its own intrinsic secondary structure propensities.
evidence: The claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data and analysis.

claim: Each CSP motif behaves as an independent unit with its own intrinsic secondary structure propensities.
source: Therefore, in both PfCSP and PbCSP we conclude that there is no discernable cooperativity between the structures of different repeat motifs, and as such, in the absence of extended or nonlocal secondary structure, each of these motifs behaves as an independent unit with its own intrinsic secondary structure propensities.
evidence: The claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data and analysis.

claim: The majority of contacts in CSP peptides are in the form of pseudo α-turns and β-turns, with backbone NH groups donating to sidechain O atoms.
source: To examine the influence of Asn, Asp, and Gln sidechains on the conformational ensemble of the peptides, we computed contact maps for backbone-sidechain hydrogen bonds (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 1). We found that the majority of contacts are in the form of pseudo α-turns and β-turns, with backbone NH groups donating to sidechain O atoms.
evidence: The claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Transient sidechain contacts do not have a stabilizing effect on backbone-backbone hydrogen bonds and are not correlated with the presence of these bonds.
source: Notably, we discovered that these transient sidechain contacts do not have a stabilizing effect on backbone-backbone hydrogen bonds and consequently, are not correlated with the presence of these bonds (numerical example in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data and analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B and C.

claim: BLI studies indicated that 3D11 Fab binds PbCSP with complex kinetics, but overall high affinity.
source: Our biolayer interferometry (BLI) studies indicated that 3D11 Fab binds PbCSP with complex kinetics, but overall high affinity (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by BLI experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: ITC indicated a high affinity interaction between 3D11 Fab and PbCSP, with a KD value of 159 ± 47 nM.
source: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) also indicated a high affinity interaction, with a KD value of 159 ± 47 nM (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: ITC revealed a very high binding stoichiometry (N = 10 ± 1), suggesting that approximately ten copies of 3D11 Fab bound one molecule of PbCSP simultaneously.
source: In addition, ITC revealed a very high binding stoichiometry (N = 10 ± 1), suggesting that approximately ten copies of 3D11 Fab bound one molecule of PbCSP simultaneously.
evidence: The claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: SEC-MALS characterization of the 3D11 Fab-PbCSP complex confirmed the high binding stoichiometry with a molecular weight of 587 ± 7 kDa for the complex.
source: Size-exclusion chromatography coupled with multi-angle light scattering (SEC-MALS) characterization of the 3D11 Fab-PbCSP complex confirmed the high binding stoichiometry with a molecular weight of 587 ± 7 kDa for the complex (Figure 2C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by SEC-MALS experimental data shown in Figure 2C-D.

claim: The SEC-MALS molecular weight is consistent with approximately eleven 3D11 Fabs bound to one molecule of PbCSP.
source: This size is consistent with approximately eleven 3D11 Fabs bound to one molecule of PbCSP, and thus, is in agreement with the results from the ITC studies within experimental error.
evidence: The claim is supported by SEC-MALS experimental data and comparison with ITC results.

claim: mAb 3D11 does not bind the PbCSP C-terminal domain (residues 202–318).
source: We first conducted BLI studies to confirm that mAb 3D11 does not bind the PbCSP C-terminal domain (residues 202–318; Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by BLI experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: mAb 3D11 preferentially binds the NPND and Mixed peptides with high affinity (KD = 45 ± 15 nM and 44 ± 4 nM, respectively).
source: Our experiments revealed that mAb 3D11 preferentially binds the NPND and Mixed peptides with high affinity (KD = 45 ± 15 nM and 44 ± 4 nM, respectively), but also binds the NAND and PAPP peptides, albeit with lower affinity (KD = 207 ± 1 nM and 611 ± 139 nM, respectively).
evidence: The claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: mAb 3D11 binds the NAND and PAPP peptides with lower affinity (KD = 207 ± 1 nM and 611 ± 139 nM, respectively).
source: Our experiments revealed that mAb 3D11 preferentially binds the NPND and Mixed peptides with high affinity (KD = 45 ± 15 nM and 44 ± 4 nM, respectively), but also binds the NAND and PAPP peptides, albeit with lower affinity (KD = 207 ± 1 nM and 611 ± 139 nM, respectively).
evidence: The claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The structure of the 3D11 Fab-NPND complex was determined at 2.30 Å resolution.
source: The structure of the 3D11 Fab-NPND complex was determined at 2.30 Å resolution, while the structures of 3D11 Fab in complex with each of the other three peptides were all solved at ~1.60 Å resolution (Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by X-ray crystallography data reported in Table 1.

claim: The structures of 3D11 Fab in complex with PAPP, NAND, and Mixed peptides were all solved at ~1.60 Å resolution.
source: The structure of the 3D11 Fab-NPND complex was determined at 2.30 Å resolution, while the structures of 3D11 Fab in complex with each of the other three peptides were all solved at ~1.60 Å resolution (Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by X-ray crystallography data reported in Table 1.

claim: All four PbCSP peptides adopted almost identical conformations when bound by 3D11 Fab.
source: Interestingly, all four peptides adopted almost identical conformations when bound by 3D11 Fab (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1), fitting deep into the binding groove and forming a curved, U-shaped structure (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by X-ray crystallography data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The PbCSP peptides fit deep into the 3D11 Fab binding groove and form a curved, U-shaped structure.
source: Interestingly, all four peptides adopted almost identical conformations when bound by 3D11 Fab (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1), fitting deep into the binding groove and forming a curved, U-shaped structure (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by X-ray crystallography data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The mAb 3D11 core epitope consisted of eight residues [PN(A/P)NDP(A/P)P] with an all-atom RMSD <0.5 Å.
source: Amongst all four peptides, the mAb 3D11 core epitope consisted of eight residues [PN(A/P)NDP(A/P)P] with an all-atom RMSD <0.5 Å.
evidence: The claim is supported by X-ray crystallography data analysis.

claim: Aromatic side chains in the mAb 3D11 CDRs form favorable pi-stacking and hydrophobic cage interactions around each PbCSP peptide.
source: Importantly, this shared recognition mode ideally positions aromatic side chains in the mAb 3D11 complementarity determining regions (CDRs) to form favorable pi-stacking and hydrophobic cage interactions around each PbCSP peptide (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by X-ray crystallography data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The majority of contacts between mAb 3D11 and PbCSP peptides are made with residues that are conserved between all four PbCSP repeat peptides.
source: Indeed, the majority of these contacts are made with residues that are conserved between all four PbCSP repeat peptides, and thus, contribute to the cross-reactive binding profile of mAb 3D11.
evidence: The claim is supported by X-ray crystallography data analysis.

claim: More van der Waals contacts were formed by a Pro residue in the PPPP and NPND motifs compared to an Ala at the same position in the PAPP and NAND motifs.
source: Our crystal structures revealed that more van der Waals contacts were formed by a Pro residue in the PPPP and NPND motifs compared to an Ala at the same position in the PAPP and NAND motifs (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by X-ray crystallography data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The epitopes of the NAND, NPND and Mixed peptides had a slightly greater buried surface area (753, 762, and 765 Å2, respectively) than the PAPP peptide (743 Å2).
source: Consequently, the epitopes of the NAND, NPND and Mixed peptides had a slightly greater buried surface area (BSA; 753, 762, and 765 Å2, respectively) than the PAPP peptide (743 Å2), which only consists of Ala-containing motifs (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by X-ray crystallography data analysis reported in Supplementary file 2.

claim: Pro10 of the PPPP motif forms more van der Waals interactions with antibody residues H.Asn33 and H.Tyr52 compared to Ala10 of the PAPP motif.
source: In particular, Pro10 of the PPPP motif found in the NAND and NPND peptides forms more van der Waals interactions with antibody residues H.Asn33 and H.Tyr52 compared to Ala10 of the PAPP motif present in PAPP and Mixed peptides.
evidence: The claim is supported by X-ray crystallography data analysis reported in Supplementary file 2.

claim: Pro6 of the NPND motif makes additional interactions with antibody residue K.Leu50 that are not present for Ala6 of the NAND motif.
source: Similarly, Pro6 of the NPND motif in the NPND and Mixed peptides makes additional interactions with antibody residue K.Leu50 that are not present for Ala6 of the NAND motif within the PAPP and NAND peptides (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by X-ray crystallography data analysis reported in Supplementary file 2.

claim: The PbCSP peptides that bury more surface area in the 3D11 paratope have the highest binding affinities.
source: These differences in interactions observed at the atomic level directly relate to the binding affinities measured by ITC, where the PbCSP peptides that bury more surface area in the 3D11 paratope have the highest binding affinities (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation between X-ray crystallography data and ITC binding affinity measurements.

claim: A dataset of 165,747 3D11 Fab-PbCSP particle images was refined with no symmetry imposed, resulting in a 3.2 Å resolution reconstruction.
source: A dataset of 165,747 3D11 Fab-PbCSP particle images was refined with no symmetry imposed, resulting in a 3.2 Å resolution reconstruction of 3D11 Fabs peripherally arranged around PbCSP with their variable domains clustered around a central density (Figure 4, Table 2 , and Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by cryoEM data shown in Figure 4, Table 2, and supplementary figures.

claim: The cryoEM map shows 3D11 Fabs peripherally arranged around PbCSP with their variable domains clustered around a central density.
source: A dataset of 165,747 3D11 Fab-PbCSP particle images was refined with no symmetry imposed, resulting in a 3.2 Å resolution reconstruction of 3D11 Fabs peripherally arranged around PbCSP with their variable domains clustered around a central density (Figure 4, Table 2 , and Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by cryoEM data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Only the density for the seven central Fabs was strong enough to warrant building a molecular model.
source: Although the low-pass filtered (20 Å) cryoEM map of the 3D11 Fab-PbCSP complex contains visible density for >10 3D11 Fabs (Figure 4—figure supplement 2F), only the density for the seven central Fabs was strong enough to warrant building a molecular model.
evidence: The claim is supported by cryoEM data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2F.

claim: 3D Variability Analysis revealed continuous flexibility at the N- and C-termini of the 3D11 Fab-PbCSP complex.
source: Indeed, 3D Variability Analysis (Punjani and Fleet, 2020) in cryoSPARC v2 (Punjani et al., 2017) revealed continuous flexibility at the N- and C-termini of the 3D11 Fab-PbCSP complex (Figure 4—video 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by 3D Variability Analysis of cryoEM data.

claim: The PbCSP repeat forms the core of the complex and is arranged into a triangular spiral of 51 Å pitch and 16 Å diameter.
source: The PbCSP repeat forms the core of the complex and is arranged into a triangular spiral of 51 Å pitch and 16 Å diameter (Figure 4B–C), which fits 61 of the 108 residues in the PbCSP central region.
evidence: The claim is supported by cryoEM data shown in Figure 4B-C.

claim: The PbCSP spiral fits 61 of the 108 residues in the PbCSP central region.
source: The PbCSP repeat forms the core of the complex and is arranged into a triangular spiral of 51 Å pitch and 16 Å diameter (Figure 4B–C), which fits 61 of the 108 residues in the PbCSP central region.
evidence: The claim is supported by cryoEM data and model building.

claim: The density in the PbCSP spiral was assigned to the high-affinity PPPPNPND repeats.
source: We assigned the density to the high-affinity PPPPNPND repeats.
evidence: The claim is supported by cryoEM data analysis and model building.

claim: The angle between two Fab variable domains is ~126°, such that approximately three Fabs are required to complete one full turn of the spiral.
source: The angle between two Fab variable domains is ~126o, such that approximately three Fabs are required to complete one full turn of the spiral (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by cryoEM data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The cryoEM structure of the 3D11 Fab-PbCSP complex and the crystal structures of the 3D11 Fab-peptide complexes are in remarkable agreement for both the Fab (backbone RMSD = 0.69 Å) and the PbCSP repeat region (backbone RMSD = 0.66 Å).
source: The cryoEM structure of the 3D11 Fab-PbCSP complex and the crystal structures of the 3D11 Fab-peptide complexes are in remarkable agreement for both the Fab (backbone RMSD = 0.69 Å) and the PbCSP repeat region (backbone RMSD = 0.66 Å; Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of cryoEM and X-ray crystallography data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Minor differences exist in the N- and C-termini of the peptides between crystal and cryoEM structures, presumably because the termini are largely unrestricted in the crystal structures compared to the cryoEM structure.
source: Minor differences exist in the N- and C-termini of the peptides, presumably because the termini are largely unrestricted in the crystal structures compared to the cryoEM structure.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of cryoEM and X-ray crystallography data and structural reasoning.

claim: 3D11 Fabs are closely arranged against one another in the 3D11 Fab-PbCSP complex to access their repeating and densely-packed epitopes.
source: To access their repeating and densely-packed epitopes, 3D11 Fabs are closely arranged against one another in the 3D11 Fab-PbCSP complex.
evidence: The claim is supported by cryoEM data analysis.

claim: The epitope for a single 3D11 Fab can be defined by 14 residues (PPPPNPNDPPPPNP), with the six C-terminal residues constituting the beginning of the epitope for the adjacent Fab.
source: Indeed, the epitope for a single Fab can be defined by 14 residues (PPPPNPNDPPPPNP, Supplementary file 3), with the six C-terminal residues constituting the beginning of the epitope for the adjacent Fab.
evidence: The claim is supported by cryoEM data analysis reported in Supplementary file 3.

claim: When considering two adjacent Fabs as a single binding unit, the BSA of the Fabs is 1313 Å2, and 1636 Å2 for PbCSP.
source: When considering two adjacent Fabs as a single binding unit, the BSA of the Fabs is 1313 Å2, and 1636 Å2 for PbCSP.
evidence: The claim is supported by cryoEM data analysis.

claim: Multiple Fab-Fab contacts are observed in the cryoEM structure.
source: Interestingly, we observe multiple Fab-Fab contacts in the cryoEM structure (Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by cryoEM data shown in Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Some of the residues involved in homotypic contacts have been somatically hypermutated (H.Tyr50 and H.Val56 in HCDR2, H.Asn58 and H.Thr73 in HC FR3, and K.Tyr27D in KCDR1).
source: Comparison of the mAb 3D11 sequence to its inferred germline precursor (IGHV1-12 and IGKV1-135) reveals that some of the residues involved in these homotypic contacts have been somatically hypermutated (H.Tyr50 and H.Val56 in HCDR2, H.Asn58 and H.Thr73 in heavy chain (HC) framework region (FR) 3, and K.Tyr27D in KCDR1; Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence analysis and cryoEM data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: H.Tyr50, H.Val56 and K.Tyr27D mediate Fab-Fab contacts in addition to directly interacting with PbCSP.
source: While H.Tyr50, H.Val56 and K.Tyr27D mediate Fab-Fab contacts in addition to directly interacting with PbCSP, H.Asn58 and H.Thr73 are only involved in Fab-Fab interactions.
evidence: The claim is supported by cryoEM data analysis.

claim: H.Asn58 and H.Thr73 are only involved in Fab-Fab interactions.
source: While H.Tyr50, H.Val56 and K.Tyr27D mediate Fab-Fab contacts in addition to directly interacting with PbCSP, H.Asn58 and H.Thr73 are only involved in Fab-Fab interactions.
evidence: The claim is supported by cryoEM data analysis.

claim: WT 3D11 Fab demonstrated significantly greater affinity for NPNDx2 compared to NPNDx1 (KD values of 45 ± 6 nM and 127 ± 32 nM, respectively).
source: Although both WT and H-58/73 germline-reverted mutant Fabs bound NPNDx1 with comparable affinity, WT 3D11 Fab demonstrated significantly greater affinity for NPNDx2 compared to NPNDx1 (KD values of 45 ± 6 nM and 127 ± 32 nM, respectively; Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The H-58/73 germline-reverted mutant bound NPNDx1 and NPNDx2 with similar affinities (KD values of 140 ± 38 nM for NPNDx2 and 160 ± 56 nM for NPNDx1).
source: On the other hand, the H-58/73 germline-reverted mutant bound each peptide with similar affinities (KD values of 140 ± 38 nM for NPNDx2 and 160 ± 56 nM for NPNDx1; Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The improved binding affinity of WT 3D11 Fab for NPNDx2 compared to NPNDx1, which is not observed for the H-58/73 germline-reverted mutant 3D11 Fab, suggests an important role for residues H.Asn58 and H.Thr73 in mediating homotypic interactions between neighboring 3D11 Fabs bound to PbCSP.
source: The improved binding affinity of WT 3D11 Fab for NPNDx2 compared to NPNDx1, which is not observed for the H-58/73 germline-reverted mutant 3D11 Fab, suggests an important role for residues H.Asn58 and H.Thr73 in mediating homotypic interactions between neighboring 3D11 Fabs bound to PbCSP.
evidence: The claim is supported by ITC experimental data and inference from the comparison of WT and mutant binding.

claim: Binding of either the 3D11 Fab or IgG can induce structural ordering of PbCSP into similar spiral conformations.
source: Comparison of nsEM 2D class averages of this 3D11 IgG-PbCSP fraction to 2D class averages of the 3D11 Fab-PbCSP complex indicated that binding of either the 3D11 Fab or IgG can induce structural ordering of PbCSP into similar spiral conformations (Figure 5—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by negative-stain EM data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Human 311 Fab and IgG in complex with PfCSP also observed the ability of both IgG and Fab to induce a spiral-like conformation in CSP.
source: Our findings are in agreement with a similar analysis previously performed with human 311 Fab and IgG in complex with PfCSP (Oyen et al., 2018), which also observed the ability of both IgG and Fab to induce a spiral-like conformation in CSP.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Oyen et al., 2018 and comparison with the current study's findings.

claim: Biophysical studies of the PfCSP central NANP repeat have shown that this region possesses low secondary structure propensities.
source: Biophysical studies of the PfCSP central NANP repeat have shown that this region possesses low secondary structure propensities (Dyson et al., 1990), and AFM studies on live Pf sporozoites suggest a range of conformations for PfCSP (Patra et al., 2017; Herrera et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Dyson et al., 1990; Patra et al., 2017; Herrera et al., 2015.

claim: AFM studies on live Pf sporozoites suggest a range of conformations for PfCSP.
source: Biophysical studies of the PfCSP central NANP repeat have shown that this region possesses low secondary structure propensities (Dyson et al., 1990), and AFM studies on live Pf sporozoites suggest a range of conformations for PfCSP (Patra et al., 2017; Herrera et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Patra et al., 2017; Herrera et al., 2015.

claim: Some of the most potent antibodies against the PfCSP repeat region are cross-reactive with the PfCSP N-terminal junction, which harbors KQPA, NPDP and NVDP motifs interspersed with NANP motifs.
source: Importantly, recent studies have uncovered that some of the most potent antibodies against the PfCSP repeat region are cross-reactive with the PfCSP N-terminal junction, which harbors KQPA, NPDP and NVDP motifs interspersed with NANP motifs (Kisalu et al., 2018; Murugan et al., 2020; Tan et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kisalu et al., 2018; Murugan et al., 2020; Tan et al., 2018.

claim: MD simulations of different sub-regions of the PfCSP central repeat, including the N-junction, provided detailed descriptions of their conformational ensemble and revealed that each sequence motif possesses a similarly low structural propensity.
source: Our MD simulations of different sub-regions of the PfCSP central repeat, including the N-junction, provided detailed descriptions of their conformational ensemble and revealed that each sequence motif possesses a similarly low structural propensity.
evidence: The claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data presented in the study.

claim: MD simulations for PbCSP indicated that the low structural propensity of central repeat motifs with subtle sequence variance extends to other Plasmodium species.
source: Our MD simulations for PbCSP also indicated that the low structural propensity of central repeat motifs with subtle sequence variance extends to other Plasmodium species.
evidence: The claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data presented in the study.

claim: These findings are in agreement with studies linking repetitive, low-complexity peptide sequences to structural disorder.
source: These findings are in agreement with studies linking repetitive, low-complexity peptide sequences to structural disorder (Rauscher and Pomès, 2012; Rauscher and Pomès, 2017; Romero et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Rauscher and Pomès, 2012; Rauscher and Pomès, 2017; Romero et al., 2001.

claim: The role of the numerous repetitive sequences observed in parasitic genomes is postulated to include maximizing parasite interactions with the target host cell, allowing the parasite to adapt under selective pressure by varying its number of repeats, and impairing the host immune response.
source: The role of the numerous repetitive sequences observed in parasitic genomes (Tan et al., 2010; Mendes et al., 2013; Davies et al., 2017) remains to be fully understood, but is postulated to include maximizing parasite interactions with the target host cell (Mendes et al., 2013), allowing the parasite to adapt under selective pressure by varying its number of repeats (Davies et al., 2017), and impairing the host immune response (Ly and Hansen, 2019; Portugal et al., 2015; Sullivan et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Tan et al., 2010; Mendes et al., 2013; Davies et al., 2017; Ly and Hansen, 2019; Portugal et al., 2015; Sullivan et al., 2015.

claim: Binding of the PfCSP repeat by inhibitory antibodies has been shown to induce various conformations in this intrinsically disordered region.
source: Binding of the PfCSP repeat by inhibitory antibodies has been shown to induce various conformations in this intrinsically disordered region (Imkeller et al., 2018; Kisalu et al., 2018; Murugan et al., 2020; Oyen et al., 2017; Tan et al., 2018; Triller et al., 2017; Scally and Julien, 2018; Pholcharee et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Imkeller et al., 2018; Kisalu et al., 2018; Murugan et al., 2020; Oyen et al., 2017; Tan et al., 2018; Triller et al., 2017; Scally and Julien, 2018; Pholcharee et al., 2020.

claim: The PbCSP repeat adopts an extended and bent conformation when recognized by inhibitory mAb 3D11.
source: Here, we show that the PbCSP repeat adopts an extended and bent conformation when recognized by inhibitory mAb 3D11.
evidence: The claim is supported by X-ray crystallography and cryoEM data presented in the study.

claim: Antibody recognition of the PfCSP repeat is often mediated by aromatic cages formed by the paratope, which surround prolines, backbone atoms, and aliphatic portions of side chains in the epitope.
source: Antibody recognition of the PfCSP repeat is often mediated by aromatic cages formed by the paratope, which surround prolines, backbone atoms, and aliphatic portions of side chains in the epitope (Murugan et al., 2020; Pholcharee et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Murugan et al., 2020; Pholcharee et al., 2020.

claim: Antibody paratope residues partaking in aromatic cages often include germline-encoded residues, such as H.Trp52 from VH3-33 signature genes that are strongly recruited in the humoral response against PfCSP.
source: Antibody paratope residues partaking in aromatic cages often include germline-encoded residues, such as H.Trp52 from VH3-33 signature genes that are strongly recruited in the humoral response against PfCSP (Julien and Wardemann, 2019; Pholcharee et al., 2020; Murugan et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Julien and Wardemann, 2019; Pholcharee et al., 2020; Murugan et al., 2018.

claim: Murine mAb 3D11 uses eight aromatic residues to recognize the PbCSP repeat.
source: Similarly, murine mAb 3D11 uses eight aromatic residues to recognize the PbCSP repeat.
evidence: The claim is supported by X-ray crystallography data analysis.

claim: Germline-encoded K.Tyr32 appears to play a central role in mAb 3D11 PbCSP recognition by contacting consecutive Asn-Asp-Pro residues (PN(A/P)NDP(A/P)P) in the middle of the core epitope, contributing 58 Å2 of BSA on the Fab.
source: Germline-encoded K.Tyr32 appears to play a central role in mAb 3D11 PbCSP recognition by contacting consecutive Asn-Asp-Pro residues (PN(A/P)NDP(A/P)P) in the middle of the core epitope, contributing 58 Å2 of BSA on the Fab.
evidence: The claim is supported by X-ray crystallography data analysis.

claim: These findings indicate a central role for germline-encoded aromatic residues in antibody binding of Plasmodium CSP repeats across species.
source: These findings indicate a central role for germline-encoded aromatic residues in antibody binding of Plasmodium CSP repeats across species.
evidence: The claim is supported by X-ray crystallography data analysis and comparison with literature on PfCSP antibodies.

claim: mAb 3D11 is cross-reactive and binds the different repeat motifs of PbCSP in nearly identical conformations.
source: Our structural and biophysical data demonstrated that mAb 3D11 is cross-reactive and binds the different repeat motifs of PbCSP in nearly identical conformations.
evidence: The claim is supported by X-ray crystallography and ITC data presented in the study.

claim: Cross-reactivity for the repeat motifs of subtle differences in PfCSP is exhibited by inhibitory human antibodies encoded by a variety of Ig-gene combinations.
source: Such cross-reactivity for the repeat motifs of subtle differences in PfCSP is also exhibited by inhibitory human antibodies encoded by a variety of Ig-gene combinations (Kisalu et al., 2018; Murugan et al., 2020; Tan et al., 2018; Triller et al., 2017; Scally et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kisalu et al., 2018; Murugan et al., 2020; Tan et al., 2018; Triller et al., 2017; Scally et al., 2018.

claim: The inferred germline precursor genes of mAb 3D11 (IGHV1-12/IGKV1-135) share the most sequence similarity with the human IGHV1-3/IGKV2-30 genes (68% and 82% sequence identity, respectively).
source: Notably, the inferred germline precursor genes of mAb 3D11 (IGHV1-12/IGKV1-135) share the most sequence similarity with the human IGHV1-3/IGKV2-30 genes (68% and 82% sequence identity, respectively); IGHV1-3 is the inferred germline precursor of the potent, cross-reactive human mAb CIS43 (Kisalu et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence analysis and citation to Kisalu et al., 2018.

claim: IGHV1-3 is the inferred germline precursor of the potent, cross-reactive human mAb CIS43.
source: Notably, the inferred germline precursor genes of mAb 3D11 (IGHV1-12/IGKV1-135) share the most sequence similarity with the human IGHV1-3/IGKV2-30 genes (68% and 82% sequence identity, respectively); IGHV1-3 is the inferred germline precursor of the potent, cross-reactive human mAb CIS43 (Kisalu et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Kisalu et al., 2018.

claim: It was previously reported that human anti-PfCSP antibody affinity is often directly associated with epitope cross-reactivity.
source: Moreover, it was previously reported that human anti-PfCSP antibody affinity is often directly associated with epitope cross-reactivity (Murugan et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Murugan et al., 2020.

claim: Most residues that mediate mAb 3D11 contacts with the PbCSP repeat are germline-encoded.
source: Most residues that mediate mAb 3D11 contacts with the PbCSP repeat are germline-encoded; indeed, of nine affinity-matured residues in the HC and three in the KC, only three are involved in direct contacts with the antigen (H.Trp50, H.Val56 and K.Tyr27D).
evidence: The claim is supported by X-ray crystallography data analysis and sequence comparison.

claim: Of nine affinity-matured residues in the HC and three in the KC, only three are involved in direct contacts with the antigen (H.Trp50, H.Val56 and K.Tyr27D).
source: Most residues that mediate mAb 3D11 contacts with the PbCSP repeat are germline-encoded; indeed, of nine affinity-matured residues in the HC and three in the KC, only three are involved in direct contacts with the antigen (H.Trp50, H.Val56 and K.Tyr27D).
evidence: The claim is supported by X-ray crystallography data analysis and sequence comparison.

claim: Due to the repetitive nature of the central repeat motifs, multiple antibodies bind simultaneously to one CSP protein and neighboring Fabs engage in homotypic interactions.
source: Due to the repetitive nature of the central repeat motifs, multiple antibodies bind simultaneously to one CSP protein and neighboring Fabs engage in homotypic interactions (Imkeller et al., 2018; Oyen et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Imkeller et al., 2018; Oyen et al., 2018, and cryoEM data from the current study.

claim: Somatic mutations of residues that partake in Fab-Fab contacts enhance homotypic interactions and indirectly improve the binding affinity of the mAb to CSP.
source: Our data suggest that somatic mutations of residues that partake in Fab-Fab contacts enhance homotypic interactions and indirectly improve the binding affinity of the mAb to CSP.
evidence: The claim is supported by cryoEM data, ITC data, and mutagenesis experiments presented in the study.

claim: mAb 3D11 recognition of PbCSP resembles binding of some neutralizing human mAbs to PfCSP.
source: In this respect, mAb 3D11 recognition of PbCSP resembles binding of some neutralizing human mAbs to PfCSP (Imkeller et al., 2018; Murugan et al., 2020; Oyen et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Imkeller et al., 2018; Murugan et al., 2020; Oyen et al., 2018, and comparison with the current study's findings.

claim: In human mAbs 311 and 1210, CDR3 regions of both heavy and light chains appear to play a considerable role in forming Fab-Fab contacts.
source: In human mAbs 311 (Oyen et al., 2018) and 1210 (Imkeller et al., 2018), CDR3 regions of both heavy and light chains appear to play a considerable role in forming Fab-Fab contacts.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Oyen et al., 2018 and Imkeller et al., 2018.

claim: In mAb 3D11, homotypic interactions are mainly mediated by residues localized in HCDR1 and −2, KCDR1, and FR3 regions of both the HC and KC, with little contribution from residues in the CDR3 regions (with the exception of H.Tyr97 in HCDR3 and K.Phe94 in KCDR3).
source: Interestingly, in the case of mAb 3D11, homotypic interactions are mainly mediated by residues localized in HCDR1 and −2, KCDR1, and FR3 regions of both the HC and KC, with little contribution from residues in the CDR3 regions (with the exception of H.Tyr97 in HCDR3 and K.Phe94 in KCDR3).
evidence: The claim is supported by cryoEM data analysis.

claim: Homotypic interactions are a feature by which the mammalian immune system can robustly engage repetitive Plasmodium antigens with high affinity in various ways.
source: Taken together, these findings indicate that homotypic interactions are a feature by which the mammalian immune system can robustly engage repetitive Plasmodium antigens with high affinity in various ways.
evidence: The claim is supported by data from the current study and comparison with literature on other anti-CSP antibodies.

claim: Recent studies have reported that Fab-Fab interactions occur in other antibody-antigen complexes, providing evidence that homotypic contacts can drive diverse biology.
source: Interestingly, recent studies have reported that Fab-Fab interactions occur in other antibody-antigen complexes, providing evidence that homotypic contacts can drive diverse biology: for example, homotypic interactions were found between two nanobodies bound to a pentameric antigen (Bernedo-Navarro et al., 2018), and between two Rituximab antibodies bound to B cell membrane protein CD20 (Rougé et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bernedo-Navarro et al., 2018 and Rougé et al., 2020.

claim: CryoEM analysis revealed how the PbCSP repeat can adopt a highly organized spiral structure upon mAb binding.
source: Our cryoEM analysis also revealed how the PbCSP repeat, like that of PfCSP, can adopt a highly organized spiral structure upon mAb binding.
evidence: The claim is supported by cryoEM data presented in the study.

claim: Spiral assembly of CSP was previously observed upon human mAb 311 Fab and IgG binding, which induced a PfCSP spiral with a greater diameter (27 Å) and smaller pitch (49 Å) compared to the 3D11-PbCSP complex (16 Å diameter and 51 Å pitch).
source: Such spiral assembly of CSP was previously observed upon human mAb 311 Fab and IgG binding, which induced a PfCSP spiral with a greater diameter (27 Å) and smaller pitch (49 Å) compared to the 3D11-PbCSP complex (16 Å diameter and 51 Å pitch) (Oyen et al., 2018; Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Oyen et al., 2018 and comparison with the current study's cryoEM data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: Differences in the architecture between the 3D11-PbCSP and 311-PfCSP complexes can be attributed to the fact that mAbs 3D11 and 311 recognize their respective antigens in distinct conformations.
source: Differences in the architecture between these two complexes can be attributed to the fact that mAbs 3D11 and 311 recognize their respective antigens in distinct conformations.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of structural data from the current study and literature.

claim: Different anti-CSP inhibitory antibodies can bind the repeat region in a variety of conformations.
source: Because different anti-CSP inhibitory antibodies can bind the repeat region in a variety of conformations (Imkeller et al., 2018; Kisalu et al., 2018; Tan et al., 2018; Triller et al., 2017; Scally and Julien, 2018), it is likely that many types of CSP-antibody assemblies exist.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Imkeller et al., 2018; Kisalu et al., 2018; Tan et al., 2018; Triller et al., 2017; Scally and Julien, 2018.

claim: It is likely that many types of CSP-antibody assemblies exist.
source: Because different anti-CSP inhibitory antibodies can bind the repeat region in a variety of conformations (Imkeller et al., 2018; Kisalu et al., 2018; Tan et al., 2018; Triller et al., 2017; Scally and Julien, 2018), it is likely that many types of CSP-antibody assemblies exist.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the variety of antibody binding modes reported in the literature.

claim: mAb 3D11 can accommodate all subtle variances of the PbCSP repeating motifs.
source: We reveal that mAb 3D11 can accommodate all subtle variances of the PbCSP repeating motifs, and, upon binding, induces structural ordering of PbCSP through homotypic interactions.
evidence: The claim is supported by X-ray crystallography and ITC data presented in the study.

claim: Upon binding, mAb 3D11 induces structural ordering of PbCSP through homotypic interactions.
source: We reveal that mAb 3D11 can accommodate all subtle variances of the PbCSP repeating motifs, and, upon binding, induces structural ordering of PbCSP through homotypic interactions.
evidence: The claim is supported by cryoEM data presented in the study.

claim: The findings uncover common mechanisms of antibody evolution in mammals against the CSP repeats of Plasmodium sporozoites.
source: Together, our findings uncover common mechanisms of antibody evolution in mammals against the CSP repeats of Plasmodium sporozoites.
evidence: The claim is based on the overall findings of the study and comparison with literature on human anti-PfCSP antibodies.
